verdict.rationale: The GST portal documents a third-party role, the GST Practitioner, with a help module on enrolling as a practitioner and accepting or rejecting a taxpayer's request. That points to a published delegation mechanism, but the pack has only a one-line mention. The DSC registration and DSC/EVC signing items describe signing methods, not which signatures stay personal to the taxpayer. missing for 10: published scope of what a practitioner may and may not do on the taxpayer's behalf, the specific authorization forms, enumeration of roles beyond the practitioner, explicit rules on which signatures or verifications cannot be delegated, independent corroboration.

support.subject: As a legal-ops lead, exactly what a third party may and may not do on my behalf is published — the authorization forms, the roles, and which signatures stay personal

citations.quote: Learn to enrol as a GST Practitioner and accept or reject a taxpayers' request.
